label: copy-phase input s (fed-back s) at recall_idx >= 3
explanation: Token detector for the letter s being fed back as input during the copy phase (i.e. the model just output an s that was original token >= 2), restricted to later copy steps. 98.6% of activation mass is on in_tok = s in the copy phase; it is silent in the original phase and at <DEL> (s in the original phase does not fire it). Magnitude grows with how late the step is: s inputs at recall_idx 2 are weak or inactive (precision of s-input at recall_idx>=2 drops to 0.76), and the strongest activations (~0.95-1.0 of max) are s inputs at the last few copy steps (to_go 0-2). Missed activations are mostly very weak (lowest quartile, 3.7% of mass) firings on other tokens late in the copy phase. It does not depend on output token, first token, or digit count.

issues: The recall_idx >= 3 cutoff misses a real class of firings. Copy-phase s inputs at recall_idx 2 with to_go <= 1 (the end of L=3/4 sequences) fire with precision 0.976 on test, which is 4.0% of active steps and 2.2% of mass. Among s at recall_idx 2, the inactive ones are at to_go >= 2: to_go 2 has precision 0.065 and to_go >= 3 has precision 0.0. So the claim 'At recall_idx 2, s inputs are weak or don't fire at all' is wrong for short sequences. What gates the feature is how late the step is, judged from both ends (recall_idx and to_go), not recall_idx alone.

There is also a to_go ceiling: no copy-phase activations at all at to_go >= 6, and s at to_go == 5 has precision only 0.19 (dev). Most remaining false positives (test misses output) are s at recall_idx 3 early in the copy phase of L=8/9 sequences (for example 'm y s j b m d 1 g <DEL> m y *s*'). The 'later the step, the stronger' description is right, but the predicate only half-encodes it.

Checked claims that hold: 98.6% of mass is on s inputs; the original phase is nearly silent (14 activations); <DEL> is silent; s with recall_idx >= 2 has precision about 0.76-0.84, depending on whether to_go is also capped; the strongest activations are at to_go 0-2. Reported test scores reproduce (P 0.935, R 0.755, F1 0.836, mass recall 0.963).

Residual misses with the improved predicate are diffuse weak non-s activations late in the copy phase (in_tok != s & to_go <= 4: precision 0.007, 1.5% of mass), so they count as scattered noise. They cap count recall at about 0.80.
